---
name: background-bash-timeout-full-verify
description: Bash run_in_background still enforces the 10-min max timeout — full verifies must be nohup-detached with a marker file + Monitor
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 8d7e2a6c-b4cb-4866-9a73-afc73d819250
---

A `Bash` call with `run_in_background: true` is still killed at the tool's max timeout (600000 ms = 10 min). The orchestrator-owned full `./mvnw clean verify` (~22 min free machine, 1–2h under memory pressure) was silently killed mid-run this way during Epic 589.

**Why:** the background flag detaches the task from the turn, not from the timeout. A 20+ min build can never finish inside it.

**How to apply:** launch long builds detached via `nohup bash -c '<build>; echo RESULT > /tmp/<marker>.txt' &` from a quick foreground Bash, then arm a `Monitor` with an until-loop on the marker file (include process-death detection: `ps -p $PID || echo DIED`). Monitor max timeout is 60 min — expect to re-arm once if the machine is loaded. Idle `spring-boot:run` dev-server JVMs don't steal CPU but hold GBs of RAM and slow the 3g-heap test JVM badly — ask the user before killing them, they usually say yes.

Related: [[subagent-stream-death-large-writes]] (the same epic hit repeated mid-stream API deaths on large Write calls — chunk to ~150 lines + Edit-append fixed it).
